host_review.background_limit: Gate uses pooled demonstration majority for background. Production dispatch cross-checks palette and fails closed on a mismatch. This is a conservative context limitation, not a proven complete inference rule for arbitrary dense scenes.
host_review.finite_hypothesis_limit: Unanimity is relative to the ten documented alignment/blocker hypotheses, not a proof against every imaginable rule. Canonical context not claimed solved.

draft_notes.author: host parallel CLI execution worker
draft_notes.explanation: Direct visible-coordinate program. It finds solid rectangles on BG=palette[0] and pairs same-colour rectangles facing across a gap. The bridge is gap x shared span with one cell trimmed at each end, painted BR=palette[8] on background. Rival rules are {centred, overlap} x {trim_any, trim_same, span_any, span_same, none}. Every rule that reproduces all demos is kept, and the program answers only if all survivors agree on the full query. Otherwise it raises Undetermined. It also raises when nothing survives, and when a bridge is needed but no demo shows its colour. D4 selects nothing.

ambiguity.intrinsic: None found. All native labels equal centred/trim_any on the visible input, for every audited pair.

draft_notes.constructor_issue: subset and expected_boxes are drawn once, outside the while-True loop, and the recursive growth must hit that count exactly. 32/200 draws exceed 5 s (rival_probe run), so the standard 5 s / 50-rejection audit cannot sample this family. The v7 audit uses a 30 s deadline, then redraws and counts the misses (see rejection_stats). Dimensions are not restricted. Proposed host fix, not applied: redraw subset/expected_boxes after K failed geometry attempts. This needs a distribution review.
